intro: Real-world economics, outside the classroom. Pick from this menu. Each approved side quest earns the Trail Volunteer badge plus 50 XP. Each one ends with a short write-up (or slideshow) explaining the economics, with photos or documents as evidence.
safetyNotes: **Ground rules:** never share real account numbers, passwords, Social Security numbers, or anyone's private financial details. Black out personal info on any document you photograph. Get a parent or guardian's OK before interviewing anyone or visiting a business.

quests.title: Price Detective
quests.task: Track the price of 5 items (gas, milk, eggs, a fast-food meal, one item you choose) at two stores for 3 weeks. Explain any changes with supply and demand.
quests.proof: Price table or chart plus a one-page explanation

quests.title: Interview an Entrepreneur
quests.task: Interview a local small-business owner: how they started, their biggest risk, their business form (sole proprietorship, LLC, etc.), and their competition.
quests.proof: Interview notes or recording summary plus a photo with the owner (with permission)

quests.title: Career Trail Map
quests.task: Research one career: training required, typical Idaho pay, job outlook, and the human capital it takes. Talk to someone who works in it if you can.

quests.title: Real Budget Month
quests.task: Track every dollar you spend for 30 days, then build a 50/30/20 budget for next month based on what you learned.
quests.proof: Spending log plus your new budget and three things you'd change

quests.title: Grocery Challenge
quests.task: Plan a week of dinners for a family of four for $120 or less, using real prices and unit prices from a local store. Include Idaho's 6% sales tax.
quests.proof: Menu, shopping list with prices, and receipt or screenshots

quests.title: Car Cost Showdown
quests.task: Compare a new car and a 4-year-old used version of the same model: price, loan payment at a credit union rate, insurance quote, gas, and depreciation over 5 years.

quests.title: Bank Account Shopper
quests.task: Compare checking and savings accounts at three institutions (include one credit union and one online bank): fees, minimums, APY, ATM access.
quests.proof: Comparison chart and which you'd pick and why

quests.title: Compound Interest Lab
quests.task: Build a spreadsheet that shows $50 a month invested from age 16 to 65 at 4%, 7%, and 10%. Compare starting at 16 vs. 26.

quests.title: College Net Price Check
quests.task: Use the net price calculator for two Idaho schools (a university and a community or technical college). Compare net price, aid, and likely loan debt for your planned career.
quests.proof: Screenshots of results plus a short comparison

quests.title: Where My Taxes Go
quests.task: Find your school district's or city's budget online. Report where the money comes from (property tax, state funds, levies) and the three biggest spending areas.
quests.proof: Pie chart or table with the source link

quests.title: Made Where?
quests.task: Check the labels on 25 items in your home. Map which countries they came from and explain one item's global supply chain.
quests.proof: Map or chart plus a photo of labels

quests.title: Idaho Export Story
quests.task: Research one Idaho export (potatoes, cheese, trout, chips, lumber, wheat): who buys it, how it gets there, and how tariffs or exchange rates affect it.
quests.proof: One-page report or slideshow with sources

quests.title: Economic Indicator Watch
quests.task: Follow the unemployment rate, inflation (CPI), and one leading indicator for a month using BLS or FRED. Predict which phase of the business cycle we're in.
quests.proof: Charts or screenshots plus your prediction with reasons

quests.title: Fed Meeting Reporter
quests.task: Read the summary of the most recent FOMC decision. Explain in your own words what the Fed decided, why, and how it could affect a family buying a car.
quests.proof: Your news-style write-up with the source link

quests.title: Scam Spotter
quests.task: Collect 5 real examples of scam texts, emails, or ads (from your family, with personal info blacked out, or from FTC alerts). Label the red flags in each.
quests.proof: Screenshots with red flags circled and explained
